# gsc command reference

This reference is generated from the command tree compiled into `gsc`. Run `make docs` after changing commands or flags.

## `gsc`

Ship Android apps to Galaxy Store from the command line.

### Usage

```text
gsc <command> [flags]
```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc auth` | Manage Galaxy Store service-account authentication. |
| `gsc apps` | View, update, and submit apps registered in Galaxy Store Seller Portal. |
| `gsc binaries` | Manage app binaries through Samsung's current v2 API. |
| `gsc uploads` | Create upload sessions and stream files to Samsung. |
| `gsc beta` | Manage Galaxy Store closed beta testers. |
| `gsc rollouts` | Manage Galaxy Store staged rollout rates and binaries. |
| `gsc reviews` | List Galaxy Store buyer comments and manage seller replies. |
| `gsc iap` | Manage Galaxy Store in-app products, transactions, subscriptions, and receipts. |
| `gsc stats` | Query Galaxy Store seller and app statistics. |
| `gsc api` | Call a documented Galaxy Store Developer API path safely. |
| `gsc doctor` | Diagnose local configuration and existing Galaxy Store credentials. |
| `gsc capabilities` | Show supported Galaxy Store API operations and Seller Portal boundaries. |
| `gsc search` | Search supported Galaxy Store operations and their gsc commands. |
| `gsc schema` | Describe the embedded curated API catalog and its provenance. |
| `gsc version` | Print version information. |

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--version` | `false` | Print version information and exit |

## `gsc auth`

Manage Galaxy Store service-account authentication.

### Usage

```text
gsc auth <command> [flags]
```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc auth login` | Exchange a service-account JWT and store the resulting token securely. |
| `gsc auth status` | Validate the resolved stored access token with Samsung. |
| `gsc auth revoke` | Revoke a token remotely, then remove it from secure local storage. |

## `gsc auth login`

Exchange a service-account JWT and store the resulting token securely.

### Usage

```text
gsc auth login --profile NAME --service-account-id ID --private-key PATH --scope SCOPE [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate inputs and show planned operations without changing state |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--private-key string` | `` | Required path to the Samsung RSA private key |
| `--profile string` | `` | Required profile name for secure token storage |
| `--scope value` | `` | Required service-account scope; repeat for publishing and gss |
| `--service-account-id string` | `` | Required Samsung service account ID |
| `--set-default` | `false` | Make this the default profile |

## `gsc auth status`

Validate the resolved stored access token with Samsung.

### Usage

```text

```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## `gsc auth revoke`

Revoke a token remotely, then remove it from secure local storage.

### Usage

```text

```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm permanent remote token revocation |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and show the revocation plan without changing state |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Required credential profile whose token will be revoked |

## `gsc apps`

View, update, and submit apps registered in Galaxy Store Seller Portal.

### Usage

```text
gsc apps <command> [flags]
```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc apps list` | List apps registered by the resolved Galaxy Store seller. |
| `gsc apps view` | View every SALE and REGISTRATION record for one app. |
| `gsc apps update` | Update Galaxy Store metadata while preserving JSON tri-state semantics. |
| `gsc apps submit` | Submit a REGISTERING app for Galaxy Store review. |
| `gsc apps status` | Change app distribution status. |

## `gsc apps list`

List apps registered by the resolved Galaxy Store seller.

Samsung returns the complete contentList array without server pagination.
--offset and --limit select a local page without inventing API query parameters.

Examples:
  gsc apps list
  gsc apps list --profile production --output table
  gsc apps list --offset 50 --limit 50 --output json

### Usage

```text
gsc apps list [--profile NAME] [--offset N] [--limit N] [--output FORMAT]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit int` | `0` | Maximum results to return; zero returns all remaining apps |
| `--offset int` | `0` | Zero-based local result offset |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc apps view`

View every SALE and REGISTRATION record for one app.

Samsung can return a published SALE record and an in-progress REGISTRATION
record for the same content ID. This command preserves both and retains unknown
response fields in JSON output.

Examples:
  gsc apps view --content-id 000007654321
  gsc apps view --content-id 000007654321 --output markdown

### Usage

```text
gsc apps view --content-id ID [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc beta testers`

List or update Samsung accounts in a closed beta.

### Usage

```text

```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc beta testers list` | List one page of closed beta testers. |
| `gsc beta testers update` | Add or remove closed beta testers from a JSON update file. |

## `gsc beta testers list`

List one page of closed beta testers.

--app-status is always explicit because SALE and REGISTRATION records can exist
simultaneously for the same content ID.

Example:
  gsc beta testers list --content-id 000007654321 --app-status REGISTRATION --output table

### Usage

```text
gsc beta testers list --content-id ID --app-status STATUS [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-status string` | `` | Required app variant: SALE or REGISTRATION |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--limit int` | `1000` | Maximum beta testers to return (1-1000) |
| `--offset int` | `0` | Zero-based beta tester offset |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc beta testers update`

Add or remove closed beta testers from a JSON update file.

The file accepts betaTestersToBeAdded, betaTestersToBeDeleted, and an optional
feedbackChannel. Samsung accepts at most 1,000 additions and 1,000 deletions per
request and can report individual invalid Samsung account IDs.

Examples:
  gsc beta testers update --content-id 000007654321 --file testers.json --dry-run
  gsc beta testers update --content-id 000007654321 --file testers.json --confirm

### Usage

```text
gsc beta testers update --content-id ID --file update.json [--dry-run | --confirm] [flags]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm the remote tester update |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and print the mutation plan without opening a session |
| `--file string` | `` | Required JSON update file |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc rollouts rate update`

Enable or monotonically advance rollout rates from JSON.

The file contains rolloutRate and an optional countries array. Before writing,
gsc reads Samsung's current rate and refuses default or country decreases.

Examples:
  gsc rollouts rate update --content-id 000007654321 --app-status SALE --file rates.json --dry-run
  gsc rollouts rate update --content-id 000007654321 --app-status SALE --file rates.json --confirm

### Usage

```text
gsc rollouts rate update --content-id ID --app-status STATUS --file rates.json [--dry-run | --confirm]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-status string` | `` | Required app variant: SALE or REGISTRATION |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm the rollout-rate mutation |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and print the mutation plan without opening a session |
| `--file string` | `` | Required JSON rollout-rate file |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc rollouts rate complete`

Complete a staged rollout by deploying to all users globally.

Samsung calls this DISABLE_ROLLOUT, but it does not stop distribution: it makes
the release available to 100% of users. gsc names the operation complete to
preserve that safety-critical meaning.

Example:
  gsc rollouts rate complete --content-id 000007654321 --app-status SALE --confirm

### Usage

```text
gsc rollouts rate complete --content-id ID --app-status STATUS [--dry-run | --confirm]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--app-status string` | `` | Required app variant: SALE or REGISTRATION |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm global completion of the rollout |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and print the mutation plan without opening a session |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc reviews`

List Galaxy Store buyer comments and manage seller replies.

### Usage

```text
gsc reviews <command> [flags]
```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc reviews list` | List buyer comments for one Galaxy Store app. |

## `gsc reviews list`

List buyer comments for one Galaxy Store app.

--comment-id filters for one exact comment. --page selects one Samsung response
page; --paginate retrieves each page and emits a lossless JSON array of the
original page responses.

Examples:
  gsc reviews list --content-id 000005021191
  gsc reviews list --content-id 000005021191 --page 2 --output table
  gsc reviews list --content-id 000005021191 --paginate --output json

### Usage

```text
gsc reviews list --content-id ID [--comment-id ID] [--page N] [--paginate] [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--comment-id string` | `` | Return one exact 7-digit buyer comment ID |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--page int` | `1` | Comment page number to retrieve |
| `--paginate` | `false` | Retrieve every page starting at --page |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc reviews reply`

Add a seller reply to one buyer comment.

Samsung permits only one reply per comment. To replace a reply, delete it
explicitly first, then create the new reply.

Examples:
  gsc reviews reply --content-id 000005021191 --comment-id 5501581 --country-code USA --body "Thank you" --dry-run
  gsc reviews reply --content-id 000005021191 --comment-id 5501581 --country-code USA --body "Thank you" --confirm

### Usage

```text
gsc reviews reply <command> [flags]
```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc reviews reply delete` | Delete the seller reply attached to one buyer comment. |

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--body string` | `` | Required seller reply text, up to 1400 UTF-8 bytes |
| `--comment-id string` | `` | Required 7-digit buyer comment ID |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm creation of the seller reply |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--country-code string` | `` | Required 3-letter uppercase Galaxy Store country code |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and show the reply plan without changing state |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc reviews reply delete`

Delete the seller reply attached to one buyer comment.

The command resolves Samsung's reply ID by reading the exact buyer comment,
then sends one confirmed delete request. It never retries the mutation.

Examples:
  gsc reviews reply delete --content-id 000005021191 --comment-id 5501581 --dry-run
  gsc reviews reply delete --content-id 000005021191 --comment-id 5501581 --confirm

### Usage

```text
gsc reviews reply delete --content-id ID --comment-id ID [--dry-run | --confirm] [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--comment-id string` | `` | Required 7-digit buyer comment ID whose reply will be deleted |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm permanent deletion of the seller reply |
| `--content-id string` | `` | Required 12-digit Galaxy Store content ID |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and show the deletion plan without changing state |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc iap purchases`

## `gsc iap purchases consume`

Consume a completed Samsung IAP purchase.

Use --purchased-id repeatedly to include Samsung's optional purchasedIdList
batch body. A dry-run performs no credential resolution or network request.

Examples:
  gsc iap purchases consume --package-name com.example.app --purchase-id PURCHASE --dry-run
  gsc iap purchases consume --package-name com.example.app --purchase-id PURCHASE --confirm

### Usage

```text
gsc iap purchases consume --package-name PACKAGE --purchase-id ID [--purchased-id ID ...] [--dry-run | --confirm] [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm purchase processing |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and show the mutation plan without changing state |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--package-name string` | `` | Required application package name |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |
| `--purchase-id string` | `` | Required Samsung purchase transaction ID |
| `--purchased-id value` | `` | Additional purchase ID for batch processing; repeat as needed |

## `gsc iap orders list`

View up to 100 Samsung IAP payment and refund records.

Samsung defines this read-only operation as POST. It never changes order state,
so --confirm and --dry-run are intentionally not part of this command.

Examples:
  gsc iap orders list --seller-seq 000123456789
  gsc iap orders list --seller-seq 000123456789 --request-date 20260730 --output json

### Usage

```text
gsc iap orders list --seller-seq ID [--package-name PACKAGE] [--request-date YYYYMMDD] [--continuation-token TOKEN] [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--continuation-token string` | `` | Optional token returned by the previous page |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--package-name string` | `` | Optional application package name |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |
| `--request-date string` | `` | Optional payment/refund date in YYYYMMDD; defaults to yesterday |
| `--seller-seq string` | `` | Required 12-digit Seller Portal deeplink number |

## `gsc api`

Call a documented Galaxy Store Developer API path safely.

### Usage

```text
gsc api <command> [flags]
```

### Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `gsc api request` | Send one authenticated request to an allowlisted Samsung API path. |

## `gsc api request`

Send one authenticated request to an allowlisted Samsung API path.

Only relative paths under Samsung's documented /seller, /iap, /gss, and token
validation/revocation endpoints are accepted. Authentication headers are always
resolved by gsc and cannot be overridden. Mutating requests require --confirm
and are never retried.

Examples:
  gsc api request --method GET --path '/seller/contentInfo?contentId=000007654321'
  gsc api request --method POST --path /gss/query/contentMetric --file query.json --confirm
  gsc api request --method PATCH --path /iap/v6/applications/com.example/items --file update.json --dry-run

### Usage

```text
gsc api request --method METHOD --path PATH [--file JSON] [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT] [--dry-run | --confirm]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--confirm` | `false` | Confirm a POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE request |
| `--dry-run` | `false` | Validate and print the request plan without opening a session |
| `--file string` | `` | Optional regular file containing one JSON request value |
| `--method string` | `` | Required HTTP method: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--path string` | `` | Required relative Samsung Developer API path, beginning with / |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |

## `gsc doctor`

Diagnose local configuration and existing Galaxy Store credentials.

By default, every check is local and no token is minted or sent over the
network. Pass --remote to validate an existing access token with Samsung.
Private keys, private-key paths, access tokens, and authorization headers are
never included in the report.

Examples:
  gsc doctor
  gsc doctor --profile production --output table
  gsc doctor --profile production --remote --output json

### Usage

```text
gsc doctor [--profile NAME] [--output FORMAT] [--remote]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
| `--profile string` | `` | Credential profile (defaults to environment or configured profile) |
| `--remote` | `false` | Validate the existing access token with Samsung |

## `gsc capabilities`

Show supported Galaxy Store API operations and Seller Portal boundaries.

The report is generated locally from gsc's embedded, audited operation catalog.
It does not contact Samsung or imply support for Seller Portal-only workflows.

Examples:
  gsc capabilities
  gsc capabilities --output json
  gsc capabilities --output table

### Usage

```text
gsc capabilities [--output <format>]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |

## `gsc search`

Search supported Galaxy Store operations and their gsc commands.

Search is local, case-insensitive, and deterministic. It matches operation IDs,
names, API families, capabilities, and proposed command strings. It does not
search apps or other live Galaxy Store data.

Examples:
  gsc search rollout
  gsc search --output json "iap subscriptions"
  gsc search --output table destructive

### Usage

```text
gsc search [--output <format>] <query>
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |

## `gsc schema`

Describe the embedded curated API catalog and its provenance.

Samsung does not publish an OpenAPI document for the Galaxy Store Developer
API. This command reports catalog metadata and field names; it does not invent
request schemas, response schemas, or undocumented endpoints.

Examples:
  gsc schema
  gsc schema --output json
  gsc schema --output markdown

### Usage

```text
gsc schema [--output <format>]
```

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--output string` | `auto` | Output format: auto, json, table, or markdown |
